clue.text: Reckless hit-and-run

parts.note: to hit someone with an open hand is to slap them
a dash is a short fast run

explanation.surface: A driver who knocks someone down and speeds off is plainly reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit-and-run' reads as one motoring crime, but split at the hyphens it gives two words, with 'and' only joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is careless and hasty, done without thought for the consequences.

clue.text: Way of Us pedestrians seems unprogressive

definitions.text: Way of Us pedestrians seems unprogressive

parts.words: Way of Us pedestrians seems unprogressive
parts.note: the American footpath beside a road, which read in two words suggests moving crabwise rather than forward

explanation.surface: American walkers seem stuck in their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Split in two the word describes walking sideways, which makes no forward progress.
explanation.definitionFit: The paved American path beside a street is the US term for a British pavement.

clue.text: Being present at finish of a race

indicators.note: finish of a race puts the finish after the race, so the race comes first

parts.note: the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
an ending is a finish

explanation.surface: A spectator is at the end of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: To be attending something is to be there in person.

clue.text: Odd as it might be, they decorate walls

indicators.note: it might be suggests these letters could be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Strange as it may seem, these are wall decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd as it might be' reads as an aside; ODD AS is the fodder, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is a decorative band or panel along the lower part of an interior wall.

clue.text: One of the top parts of play-school

definitions.text: One of the top parts of play-school

parts.words: One of the top parts of play-school
parts.note: split as surf plus ace, a champion at the play of riding waves, one of the stars of a surfing school

explanation.surface: Something counts among the best features of a nursery school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top parts' means the uppermost layer, but split the answer as SURF ACE and it is a star pupil of a surf school.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface is the outermost or uppermost layer of something.

clue.text: I'm accustomed to being diverted

parts.note: I'm stands for I am; with the speaker understood, the verb am is what remains
to be used to something is to be accustomed to it

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are well used to being entertained.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'I'm accustomed' as I AM USED with the I dropped, since the speaker is taken as given; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be amused is to be entertained, which is the old sense of diverted.

clue.text: Church leader no extremist

definitions.meaning: the presiding minister of a Presbyterian assembly, as in the Church of Scotland
one who takes a middle course in opinions

explanation.definitionFit: The chair of a Presbyterian general assembly bears this title, and someone moderate in views is also so called.

clue.text: Zealous disciple, pure and simple

definitions.meaning: ... the Zealot was one of the twelve apostles
... Pure means the genuine article, and Simple ... is the nursery-rhyme simpleton

explanation.walkthrough: 'pure and simple' is an idiom; here each word goes with the name: Simon Pure and Simple Simon.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle called the Zealot shared this name, which also completes both the phrase for the real thing and the nursery-rhyme fool.

clue.text: Tribal language of N Europe?

parts.note: Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, so a word meaning like Dan could be called tribal; it is really a Scandinavian tongue

explanation.surface: A question about some tribal tongue spoken in northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: Dan is a tribe of Israel, and -ISH means belonging to.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of Denmark is spoken in northern Europe.

clue.text: French priests hold right to be healers

indicators.note: to hold something is to contain it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cure is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: Some French clergy claim the right to heal the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: CURE is the French word for a parish priest, which English crosswords borrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who cure illness are healers.

clue.text: Having an appointment that's obsolete

definitions.meaning: someone who has a date has an arranged meeting, often a romantic one
something old-fashioned and out of use

explanation.definitionFit: One who has a romantic engagement has dated, and anything long out of fashion is also dated.

clue.text: Golfer delivers the goods?

parts.note: a golfer plays rounds, so a golfer could be called a man of rounds; the real sense is a tradesman who makes daily deliveries along a route

explanation.surface: A golfer finally plays well under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivers the goods' is an idiom for succeeding; here it is literal, the milkman or baker's man doing a delivery round, as British tradesmen did.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman doing regular door-to-door deliveries along a fixed route goes by this name.

clue.text: Beaufort nuclear plant

definitions.meaning: the Beaufort scale grades the strength of the wind from calm to hurricane
the Cumbrian nuclear site in north-west England, since renamed Sellafield

explanation.walkthrough: Windscale was the old name of the Sellafield nuclear works in Cumbria, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beaufort measure is a gauge of gale force, and the same name belonged to England's best-known atomic site.

clue.text: But they are all square in boxing terms!

definitions.text: But they are all square in boxing terms!

parts.words: But they are all square in boxing terms!
parts.note: a joke that boxing arenas, though named for circles, are actually four-sided enclosures

explanation.surface: A wry remark that fights are always even, as boxing commentators would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all square' suggests a drawn contest; it is literal, about the shape of the roped arena that is named as if round.
explanation.definitionFit: The roped enclosures where boxers fight are called by a name meaning circles though they are square.

clue.text: Lies carelessly by the river in spare time

indicators.note: something done carelessly is jumbled, so the letters of this word are rearranged

parts.note: the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Someone lounges idly beside the river when they have a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carelessly' turns LIES into LEIS; the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time away from work or duties.

clue.text: Discovered to have no safe-conduct to the ground

definitions.meaning: found by digging or searching

definitions.text: to have no safe-conduct to the ground
definitions.meaning: in electrics, an appliance lacking an earth wire has no protective path to the ground

explanation.walkthrough: In British electrical terms an earth is the wire connecting to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dug up has been found, and a device with no earth wire is also so described.

clue.text: Roman god wants other things for festival

indicators.note: to want is to lack, so the festival's name lacks a part

parts.note: the Saturnalia was the Roman midwinter feast of revelry
alia is Latin for other things, as in inter alia

explanation.surface: A Roman deity demands something different for his feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' looks like desire but means lacks: the Roman festival named after the god, without Latin ALIA, leaves the god himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn was the Roman deity of sowing and agriculture, honoured each December.

clue.text: Putting in cell to improve new engine

definitions.meaning: slang for arresting a suspect and taking them to the cells
driving a new engine gently at first so its parts wear smoothly

explanation.definitionFit: Police slang for arresting someone is this phrase, which also means gently breaking in a new motor.

clue.text: Talks incoherently of a club on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts something inside it

parts.note: on board means aboard a steamship, and SS stands for steamship
a putter is a golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: Someone babbles about a golf club while aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a convention for going inside SS, the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sputters speaks in jerky, spitting bursts, so talks incoherently.

clue.text: Came to terms for ancient roundabout

indicators.note: roundabout says one word goes around another, enclosing it

parts.note: something ancient is very old, or aged
re means concerning, so it can stand for the word for in the sense of on behalf of a subject

explanation.surface: People reached a settlement over an old traffic circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' looks like a traffic island but is the container signal; using 'for' to mean 're', as in 'concerning', is a loose old-style equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: To have agreed is to have reached an accord after negotiation.

clue.text: Sea-birds of various kinds

definitions.meaning: loons and similar water birds that dive for fish
an old word for sundry or several

explanation.definitionFit: Loons are diving water birds known by this name, and the archaic adjective means sundry.

clue.text: Plant at face value a bargain

parts.note: par is the nominal or face value of a share or bond
a snip is British slang for something going cheap

explanation.surface: A factory bought outright at its nominal price was a real bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: SNIP is British for a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a vegetable with a pale tapering root, so a plant.

clue.text: Offer here and now

definitions.meaning: to hand over or give formally
existing at this moment, not past or future

explanation.definitionFit: To hand something over formally is to give it, and the current moment is also called by this word.

clue.text: Any amount of chimneys!

definitions.meaning: informal for lots, a great deal
tall flues on factories or houses

explanation.definitionFit: Informally, lots of something is heaps of it, and tall factory flues are also called this.

clue.text: Come to point of recording, right?

parts.note: a tape is a recording made on magnetic tape

explanation.surface: A speaker is urged to get to the point of a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come to point' looks like getting to the point of the talk; it means narrowing to a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to grow gradually thinner until it ends in a tip.

clue.text: Parents about right for Violet

indicators.note: about means going around, so the parents enclose the next piece

parts.note: pa and ma are informal names for father and mother

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad are quite correct in choosing a shade of purple.
explanation.walkthrough: The Parma violet is a strongly scented violet, also a British sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parma is a fragrant double variety of violet named after the Italian city.

clue.text: Position with admirable prospects

parts.note: reads like a promising job, but describes a spot offering fine scenery

explanation.surface: A job advert for a post with excellent career prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prospects' suggests career promise; here it means views, so the place is a scenic lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot giving a fine outlook over scenery is a vantage place of this kind.

clue.text: Made close study over colour for pillar-boxes

indicators.note: colour for pillar-boxes puts the colour after the body responsible for the boxes

parts.note: PO, the Post Office, ran Britain's street post boxes
red is the colour of British post boxes

explanation.surface: Someone scrutinised the shade used for post boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: Pillar-boxes are British street post boxes, painted Post Office red.
explanation.definitionFit: To pore over something is to read or examine it intently.

clue.text: Animal worker is out of order

definitions.text: Animal worker is out of order

parts.words: Animal worker is out of order
parts.note: a draught animal that hauls wagons, whose name puts the vehicle before the beast, which is backwards

explanation.surface: A farm animal is misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'putting the cart before the horse' means doing things in the wrong order, and the name of this horse does exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy draught animal bred for hauling wagons on farms is a working beast of this name.

clue.text: Rascal of abnormal type

definitions.meaning: a scamp or scoundrel
in biology, a plant or animal differing from the norm of its kind

explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a dishonest scamp, and a specimen deviating from its variety is also called by this name.

clue.text: Holds good in first and second part

indicators.note: in, together with part, says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A rule applies in the first and second sections of a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' backs up 'in': the answer is a part of 'first and second'.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim that remains valid still stands, so holds good means stays in force.

clue.text: They learn of French participation in publicity feats

indicators.note: participation in says one part takes its place inside another

parts.note: stunts are attention-grabbing feats done for publicity
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Pupils study how the French take part in publicity stunts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'participation in' reads as taking part, but it is the container signal; 'They learn' is a definition of the plural, people who study.
explanation.definitionFit: Students are people engaged in study, so they learn.
